'''Rondae Hollis-Jefferson''' (born January 3, 1995) is an American [[basketball]] player who recently completed his college career for the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball]] team.

== Early life and high school career ==
[[File:20130403 MCDAAG Rondae Hollis-Jefferson (2).JPG|thumb|left|upright|Hollis-Jefferson in the [[2013 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]]]]
Hollis-Jefferson grew up in [[Chester, Pennsylvania]] the son of Rylanda Hollis, who worked two jobs as a dietary supervisor and bartender. He has a brother, [[Rahlir Hollis-Jefferson|Rahlir]], who played at [[Temple Owls men's basketball|Temple]] and now plays professionally in [[Luxembourg]]. Their father was frequently absent and spent some time in jail.<ref name=republic>{{cite news|last1=Boivin|first1=Paola|title=Arizona's Hollis-Jefferson knows all about sacrifice|url=http://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/college/ua/2014/03/22/arizonas-hollis-jefferson-knows-sacrifice/6761293/|accessdate=June 21, 2015|work=[[The Arizona Republic]]|date=March 25, 2014}}</ref> Rondae Hollis Jefferson began honing his game when he was 12.<ref name=noact/> At a young age he took a strong interest in defense and acknowledged that he scored only because he was taller than his peers.<ref name=republic/>

He attended [[Chester High School (Chester, Pennsylvania)|Chester High School]] where he would begin an outstanding basketball career under head coach Larry Yarbray. The [[small forward]] became the first player to ever be named [[Delaware County, Pennsylvania|Delaware County]] Player of the Year for multiple seasons.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Chandik|first1=Matt|title=Daily Times Player of the Year: Despite setback, Chester's Rondae Jefferson should be proud|url=http://www.delcotimes.com/general-news/20130328/daily-times-player-of-the-year-despite-setback-chesters-rondae-jefferson-should-be-proud|website=DelcoTimes.com|accessdate=29 June 2014}}</ref> He was also instrumental in Chester's first-ever undefeated season. The Clippers finished 91-5 in his last three years at the school and won two state titles.<ref name=cox/> In his senior year, he lost in the state title game to [[Lower Merion High School|Lower Merion]].<ref name=noact/> He finished his career with more than 1,000 points and a school-record 780 rebounds.<ref name=cox/>

Hollis-Jefferson participated in the [[2013 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2013 McDonald's All-American Game]] against future [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]] teammate, [[Aaron Gordon]].<ref>{{cite web|last1=Zimmerman|first1=Kevin|title=Aaron Gordon is 2013 McDonald's All-American MVP, Rondae Jefferson makes unconfirmed history|url=http://www.azdesertswarm.com/basketball/2013/4/3/4181580/aaron-gordon-2013-mcdonalds-all-american-mvp-rondae-jefferson|website=AZDesertsWarm.com|publisher=SBNation.com|accessdate=29 June 2014}}</ref> Following the event, he took part in the [[Jordan Brand Classic]] with some of the most highly-recruited high school stars in the nation such as [[Julius Randle]].<ref>{{cite web|last1=Breen|first1=Matt|title=Chester's Rondae Jefferson named to Jordan Brand Classic|url=http://www.philly.com/philly/blogs/rally/Chesters-Rondae-Jefferson-named-to-Jordan-Brand-Classic.html|website=Philly.com|accessdate=29 June 2014}}</ref> At the conclusion of Hollis-Jefferson's years with the Clippers, he was tabbed the 6th best [[small forward]] of his class by [[247Sports.com]] and the fifth best by [[Rivals.com]]. He eventually chose to attend the [[University of Arizona]] and represent the school through their successful [[basketball]] program over other possibilities such as [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]] and [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Rondae Hollis-Jefferson -Yahoo! Sports|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/recruiting/player-Rondae-Hollis-Jefferson-125946|website=Rivals|publisher=Yahoo! Sports|accessdate=29 June 2014}}</ref>

== College career ==
In his freshman season with Arizona, Hollis-Jefferson became known as fierce [[Point (basketball)|scorer]], [[rebound (basketball)|rebounder]], and [[block (basketball)|shot-blocker]] despite his relatively small size. The start of his season was marked with 10 points, 5 rebounds, and 2 assists against [[Cal Poly Mustangs men's basketball|Cal Poly]] off the bench. He posted his first double-double in a game against [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]].<ref name=arizona/> He improved on his [[free throw]] shooting as his freshman year progressed. Throughout the season, Hollis-Jefferson mainly functioned as the team's [[sixth man]], but became a starter after [[Brandon Ashley]] was lost for the season with a foot injury in the Wildcats' 60-58 upset loss to [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|California]] on February 1.<ref name=noact>{{cite news|last1=Santoliquito|first1=Joseph|title=Rondae Hollis-Jefferson's game is no act|url=http://www.philly.com/philly/sports/colleges/20140316_Rondae_Hollis-Jefferson_s_game_is_no_act.html#wy5C0UxJYWeDHCkk.99|accessdate=June 21, 2015|work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|date=March 16, 2014}}</ref> Hollis-Jefferson ended up starting 6 of 38 games played due to the roster that was dominated by the likes of [[Aaron Gordon]], but still got his name on the [[Pacific-12 Conference|Pac-12]] All-Freshman Team.<ref name=arizona>{{cite web|title=Rondae Hollis-Jefferson Bio|url=http://www.arizonawildcats.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=208761261|website=ArizonaWildcats.com|accessdate=29 June 2014}}</ref> In his freshman year, Hollis-Jefferson averaged 9.1 points, 5.7 rebounds, and 1.4 assists per game.<ref name=cox>{{cite news|last1=Cox|first1=Danny|title=Rondae Hollis-Jefferson Brings Arizona In The Sweet 16 With Talent And Leadership|url=http://pittsburgh.cbslocal.com/2015/03/23/rondae-hollis-jefferson-brings-arizona-in-the-sweet-16-with-talent-and-leadership/|accessdate=June 21, 2015|work=[[CBS]]|date=March 23, 2015}}</ref> "It's a lot different than just waking up, going to school and playing basketball for Chester," said Hollis-Jefferson of his freshman year. "In the beginning of the season, I was lost. But it's not about who's starting, it's about who finishes. It stuck with me for about a month or so, playing behind people. I went along with it and kept playing. I need to make people respect my shot. I know I can shoot it. I have to stay in attack mode."<ref name=noact/>

Hollis-Jefferson increased his averages as a sophomore to 11.3 points and 6.9 rebounds per game. He improved in his leadership and offense.<ref name=cox/> As a sophomore, he was voted first-team [[List of All-Pacific-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]], and was named to the Pac-12 All-Defensive Team.<ref>{{cite press release|title=2014-15 Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Honors|date=March 9, 2015|publisher=Pac-12|url=http://pac-12.com/article/2015/03/09/2014-15-pac-12-conference-mens-basketball-honors|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6WuCA8C5K|archivedate=March 9, 2015|deadurl=no}}</ref> He helped lead the Wildcats to two consecutive Elite Eight appearances in the NCAA Tournament, losing to [[Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball|Wisconsin]] on both occasions. On April 7, 2015, Hollis-Jefferson declared for the [[2015 NBA draft]], forgoing his final two years of college eligibility. "I don't know if I've enjoyed coaching a player more than I've enjoyed coaching Rondae," coach [[Sean Miller]] said.<ref>{{cite web|title=Hollis-Jefferson leaving Arizona, declares for NBA Draft|url=http://www.foxsports.com/arizona/story/rondae-hollis-jefferson-leaving-arizona-declares-for-nba-draft-040715|publisher=Fox Sports|accessdate=20 June 2015}}</ref>
